check.reason: The patient angle is fine: the target is the system, and the forms line sympathizes with patients. The problem is invented specifics. The real headline says only that state officials are meeting to swap notes. Our headline adds 'Maryland' and upgrades 'state officials' to 'Medicaid Directors', and the take adds 'behind closed doors'. None of these is supported by the headline we were given, so they risk misstating the story. 'Unreleased homework' also implies missing federal guidance that the headline doesn't mention. Remove or verify the location, the title and the closed-door detail, and keep the joke about officials comparing notes on a policy that is already law.

pick.title: State officials scrambling to implement Medicaid work requirements meet up to swap notes
pick.headline: Medicaid Directors Convene in Maryland to Compare Notes on Unreleased Homework
pick.take: State officials are gathering behind closed doors to figure out how to verify work requirements that are already law. Nothing says confidence in a policy like a conference where everyone asks what the others are doing. The patients, as usual, will be the ones filling out the forms.
